questions.question_text: Define the Internet. Explain its development and popular services.

answer_key.model_answer: The Internet is a global network connecting millions and billions of computers throughout the world. Users communicate through the standard Internet protocol suite TCP/IP. It uses wireless, networking and electronic technologies to exchange information. According to the notes, DARPA developed the Internet and it was connected for the first time in 1969. Popular services include the World Wide Web, email, social media, online games and software updates.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark definition; 2 marks TCP/IP and technologies; 1 mark DARPA and 1969; 2 marks any four services.
answer_key.important_keywords: global network, TCP/IP, DARPA, 1969, WWW, email, social media, online games, software updates

questions.question_text: What is a web browser? Explain its functions and give examples.

answer_key.model_answer: A web browser is a software application used to access information on the World Wide Web. When a user requests information, the browser fetches data from a web server and displays the web page. Its functions include retrieving information, visiting websites using URLs, supporting plugins, following hyperlinks, storing data in internal cache and opening multiple web pages at the same time. Examples include WorldWideWeb, Netscape Navigator, Internet Explorer, Firefox and Google Chrome.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark definition; 3 marks functions; 2 marks examples.
answer_key.important_keywords: web browser, retrieve information, URL, plugins, hyperlinks, cache, multiple webpages, Chrome, Firefox

questions.question_text: Define a web server. Explain how a web server works.

answer_key.model_answer: A web server is a computer where web content is stored. It is mainly used to host websites, but web servers can also support gaming, storage, FTP and email. A web server responds to a client request in two ways: it sends the file associated with the requested URL, or it generates a response by invoking a script and communicating with a database.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition and uses; 2 marks sending requested file; 2 marks script and database response.
answer_key.important_keywords: web server, web content, hosting, client request, URL, script, database

questions.question_text: What is a URL? Explain its syntax and all its components with an example.

answer_key.model_answer: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator. It is used to address a document or other data on the web. Its general syntax is scheme://prefix.domain:port/path/filename. Scheme defines the Internet service such as HTTP or HTTPS. Prefix defines a domain prefix. Domain is the Internet domain name. Port is the port number at the host; HTTP commonly uses port 80 by default. Path identifies a location on the server. Filename identifies the document or resource.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark definition; 1 mark syntax; 4 marks explanation of components.
answer_key.important_keywords: Uniform Resource Locator, scheme, prefix, domain, port, path, filename, HTTP

questions.question_text: Define URI. Differentiate between URI and URL.

answer_key.model_answer: URI stands for Uniform Resource Identifier. It is a string of characters used to identify a name or a resource. A URI identifies and distinguishes a resource by its name or location. URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator and identifies the location or address of a resource on the web. URI includes URN and URL as subsets; every URL is a URI, but every URI is not a URL. An ISBN is an example of URI, while https://www.javatpoint.com is an example of URL.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark URI definition; 2 marks URI purpose and subsets; 3 marks correct differences and examples.
answer_key.important_keywords: Uniform Resource Identifier, Uniform Resource Locator, identify, location, URN, every URL is URI, ISBN

questions.question_text: What is HTTP? Explain its features.

answer_key.model_answer: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol. It is used to access data on the World Wide Web. It can transfer plain text, hypertext, audio, video and other data. Its features are: connectionless, media independent and stateless. Connectionless means the connection exists only during the current request and response. Media independent means different data can be sent if both client and server can handle it. Stateless means the client and server do not retain information between separate requests.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark full form and use; 3 marks features; 2 marks explanations.
answer_key.important_keywords: HyperText Transfer Protocol, connectionless, media independent, stateless, request, response, MIME

questions.question_text: Explain the HTTP transaction between a client and a server.

answer_key.model_answer: An HTTP transaction takes place between a client and a server. First, the client initiates the transaction by sending a request message to the server. The server receives and processes the request. After processing, the server sends a response message back to the client. Thus, the main steps are request message from client and response message from server.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark introduction; 2 marks client request; 2 marks server processing and response; 1 mark sequence.
answer_key.important_keywords: HTTP transaction, client, server, request message, response message

questions.question_text: What is SMTP? Explain its purpose and components.

answer_key.model_answer: SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. It is a set of communication guidelines used by software to transmit electronic mail over the Internet. It allows messages to be sent to one or more recipients and supports message content such as text, voice, video and graphics. Its two main components are User Agent (UA) and Mail Transfer Agent (MTA). The UA prepares the message and creates the envelope. The MTA transfers the mail across the Internet.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark full form; 2 marks purpose; 3 marks UA and MTA.
answer_key.important_keywords: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, email, User Agent, UA, Mail Transfer Agent, MTA, envelope

questions.question_text: Explain the working of SMTP in detail.

answer_key.model_answer: SMTP working includes five stages. 1. Composition of mail: the user writes an email using a Mail User Agent; the message contains a header and body. 2. Submission: the mail client submits the email to the SMTP server using TCP port 25, as stated in the notes. 3. Delivery: the Mail Transfer Agent checks the recipient domain and uses the MX record in DNS to find the target domain. 4. Receipt and processing: the incoming server or Mail Delivery Agent stores the email. 5. Access and retrieval: the user retrieves the stored email using a Mail User Agent with login and password.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark composition; 1 mark submission; 2 marks delivery and MX record; 1 mark receipt; 1 mark retrieval.
answer_key.important_keywords: composition, header, body, TCP port 25, MTA, MX record, DNS, MDA, MUA

questions.question_text: What is FTP? Explain its advantages and disadvantages.

answer_key.model_answer: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol. It is a standard Internet protocol provided by TCP/IP and is used to transfer files from one host to another. It is used to transfer web page files to servers and download files. Advantages include speed, efficiency, login-based access using username and password, and two-way file movement. Disadvantages include that not all providers encrypt transmissions, the notes mention a 2 GB file-size limit, simultaneous transfers to multiple receivers are not supported, passwords and contents may be sent in clear text, and it is not compatible with every system.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark full form and definition; 2 marks uses; 1.5 marks advantages; 1.5 marks disadvantages.
answer_key.important_keywords: File Transfer Protocol, TCP/IP, speed, efficient, username, password, encryption, clear text, 2GB

questions.question_text: What is HTML? Explain HyperText, Markup Language and Web Page.

answer_key.model_answer: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is used to create web pages and web applications. HyperText means text containing links that connect two or more web pages. A markup language applies layout and formatting conventions to a text document and can make text interactive by turning it into images, tables and links. A web page is a document commonly written in HTML and interpreted by a web browser. HTML can be used to create static web pages.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark full form and definition; 2 marks HyperText; 2 marks markup language; 1 mark web page.
answer_key.important_keywords: HyperText Markup Language, links, markup, layout, formatting, web page, browser, static

questions.question_text: Explain the basic structure of an HTML document with the function of each tag.

answer_key.model_answer: A basic HTML document contains , , , and <body> elements. <!DOCTYPE> defines the document type or HTML version. <html> informs the browser that the document is HTML and contains the other HTML elements. <head> contains metadata. <title> sets the page title shown in the browser window or tab. <body> contains the main visible content. <h1> defines a first-level heading and <p> defines a paragraph.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark structure; 1 mark DOCTYPE; 1 mark html; 1 mark head/title; 1 mark body; 1 mark h1/p.
answer_key.important_keywords: DOCTYPE, html, head, metadata, title, body, h1, paragraph

questions.question_text: Explain the important features of HTML.

answer_key.model_answer: HTML is easy to understand and modify. It provides formatting tags for effective presentation. It offers a flexible way to design web pages with text. The anchor tag allows links between web pages and improves browsing. HTML is platform-independent and can be displayed on Windows, Linux and Macintosh. It also supports adding graphics, videos and sound to web pages. HTML is case-insensitive, so tags can be written in uppercase or lowercase.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark introduction; 5 marks any five correctly explained features.
answer_key.important_keywords: easy, formatting tags, flexible, anchor tag, platform-independent, graphics, videos, sound, case-insensitive

questions.question_text: Explain HTML text formatting elements with suitable examples.

answer_key.model_answer: HTML formatting elements change the appearance or meaning of text. displays bold text without adding logical importance. marks important text and is generally displayed in bold. displays italic text, while gives emphasis and is generally displayed in italic. underlines text. displays smaller text. represents deleted content. displays text with a line through it. Examples: Bold, Italic, Underline.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark purpose; 4 marks explanation of tags; 1 mark examples.
answer_key.important_keywords: b, strong, i, em, u, small, del, s, formatting

questions.question_text: What are HTML hyperlinks? Explain the anchor tag and its href attribute with an example.

answer_key.model_answer: HTML links or hyperlinks connect one resource on the web to another. The resource may be a web page, image, program, video or audio clip. The tag defines a hyperlink. Its syntax is link text. The href attribute is the most important attribute because it specifies the destination of the link. The link text is visible to the reader, and clicking it opens the specified URL. Example: Visit W3Schools.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark definition; 2 marks uses; 2 marks anchor syntax and href; 1 mark example.
answer_key.important_keywords: hyperlink, anchor tag, a, href, destination, link text, URL

questions.question_text: Explain ordered and unordered lists in HTML with tags and types.

answer_key.model_answer: HTML lists organize information in ordered or unordered form. An ordered list uses the <ol> tag and displays items in a sequence. Its type values include 1, I, i, A and a. The start attribute sets the starting value, while reversed displays items in descending order. An unordered list uses the <ul> tag and displays bullet items without a particular order. Its marker types include disc, circle, square and none. The <li> tag defines each list item.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark purpose; 2 marks ordered list and types; 2 marks unordered list and types; 1 mark li tag.
answer_key.important_keywords: ordered list, ol, unordered list, ul, li, type, start, reversed, disc, circle, square

questions.question_text: What is the HTML input tag? Explain text, password and submit input types with examples.

answer_key.model_answer: The HTML <input> tag represents a form input control. It allows users to enter data and communicate with a website or application. <input type="text"> creates a single-line text field. <input type="password"> creates a password field in which entered characters are masked. <input type="submit"> creates a button that submits form data to a form-handler. Example: <input type="text" name="username">, <input type="password" name="pwd"> and <input type="submit" value="Submit">.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark input tag definition; 1.5 marks text; 1.5 marks password; 1.5 marks submit; 0.5 mark examples.
answer_key.important_keywords: input tag, form control, text, password, masked, submit, form-handler

questions.question_text: What is CSS? Explain its uses and advantages.

answer_key.model_answer: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. It is a style sheet language used to describe the look and formatting of a document written in a markup language. It is generally used with HTML to change the style of web pages and user interfaces. CSS solves the problem of repeating presentation code on every page, saves time because an external CSS file can style many pages, and provides more detailed styling attributes than plain HTML.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark full form; 1 mark definition; 2 marks uses; 2 marks advantages.
answer_key.important_keywords: Cascading Style Sheets, styling, HTML, presentation, saves time, external CSS, attributes

questions.question_text: Explain CSS rule-set syntax and the three types of CSS.

answer_key.model_answer: A CSS rule-set contains a selector and a declaration block. The selector identifies the HTML element to style. The declaration block contains one or more declarations separated by semicolons. Each declaration has a property and a value separated by a colon. Syntax: selector { property: value; }. The three types are Inline CSS, Internal CSS and External CSS. Inline CSS is written in an element's style attribute. Internal CSS is written inside the <style> tag in the head section. External CSS is stored in a separate .css file and linked to the HTML document.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark rule-set; 2 marks selector/declaration/property/value; 3 marks three CSS types.
answer_key.important_keywords: selector, declaration block, property, value, inline, internal, external, style, .css

questions.question_text: What are CSS selectors? Explain element, ID, class, universal and group selectors with examples.

answer_key.model_answer: CSS selectors select HTML elements that we want to style. The element selector selects elements by tag name, for example p. The ID selector selects a unique element and uses #, for example #para1. The class selector selects elements with a given class and uses a dot, for example .center. The universal selector uses * and selects all elements. The group selector applies the same styles to multiple selectors separated by commas, for example h1, h2, p { color: blue; }.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark definition; 1 mark each for five selectors and examples.
answer_key.important_keywords: CSS selector, element, ID, #, class, dot, universal, *, group selector, comma
